statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity index futures are still shut with the 22:00 UTC restart under three hours away, so there is no live Nasdaq-100 price path to score and Tail remains far below the block threshold, while Stress stays elevated on an unresolved US-Iran naval confrontation around the Strait of Hormuz and on September FOMC hike pricing near two-thirds heading into CPI week.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC futures-reopen window rather than across the whole outlook; existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: No live Nasdaq-100 price path under three hours before the 22:00 UTC reopen, as Tehran signals a new Hormuz restricted zone and September Fed hike odds sit near two-thirds
body: CME equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00 UTC, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path is observable at this assessment. The last verified tape remains Friday September 4: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,544.15 (+0.21%) inside a 29,440.15-29,655.22 range against a 29,482.30 previous close, a mid-range finish with no session-extreme hold. VIX ended at 14.53 (+1.47%) after a contained 13.80-14.58 range, which is not a stressed equity-volatility regime. Friday's internals were rotational rather than directional: every tracked semiconductor name rose, led by Micron, AMD and Intel, while Tesla, Apple, Microsoft and Alphabet fell. That split argues against an aligned one-way regime being carried into the reopen. The geopolitical picture escalated in wording rather than in confirmed action during the past hour. Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary said a restricted zone will be announced in the coming days, beginning at the US Navy blockade line and extending into parts of the Gulf, with any vessel entering placed on Tehran's sanctions list; separately, Iran described the Strait as completely closed with only seven or eight ships passing, while the US President posted that flows are running near 18 million barrels a day against 20 million before the conflict. Those two claims cannot both hold, and the gap between them is the main reason Confidence eases a point. This follows Saturday's CENTCOM strikes on three IRGC-linked tankers, one of which has since sunk in the Gulf of Oman, and the redirection of 92 commercial vessels. OPEC+ met on Sunday and left October quotas unchanged, pausing its unwinding of the 1.65 million barrel-per-day cut after six consecutive increases; the group next meets on October 4. Brent settled Friday at $96.28 and WTI at $82.44, crude up more than 8% on the week, with US diesel at a record $5.85 per gallon and distillate stockpiles at record lows for the season. On rates, H.15 for September 3 shows the 2-year at 4.34%, the 10-year at 4.77% and the 30-year at 5.25%, and August payrolls of 162,000 against a 53,000 consensus lifted implied odds of a September 15-16 FOMC hike from around half to roughly two-thirds. That combination keeps Stress elevated. It does not move Tail, because Tail measures an observed pathological price path and no price path exists while the venue is shut. Conditional risk is therefore concentrated in the 22:00-02:00 UTC reopen, when a two-day headline backlog would meet the thinnest depth of the week; that window maps to WATCH rather than to a block, since gap risk without observed extension is not evidence of mean-reversion failure. Monday is the US Labor Day holiday: US cash markets are closed, CME equity index futures trade a shortened session ending 17:00 UTC, and the US data calendar is empty until Tuesday. The week's high-impact checkpoints are PPI and Oracle results on September 10 and CPI on September 11, ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC that sits outside this outlook window.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available. Tail held in a narrow 4-5 band with EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress oscillated between 52 and 58 across the weekend closure, easing through the Asian overnight and firming again across the European and US Sunday hours to finish the window at its high of 58. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every hour, reflecting a closed venue rather than an observed regime.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover three further closed hours, the scheduled 22:00 UTC futures reopen, and an Asian and European session on a US Labor Day holiday with no US cash open inside the window. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band except for the two hours around the reopen, which reach 23 and 21 and map to WATCH where the unresolved Hormuz escalation, a pending Iranian restricted-zone announcement and a stretched energy complex would meet the thinnest depth of the week, before decaying toward 8 as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. Stress peaks near 67 at the reopen on the combined rates, energy and geopolitical backdrop before unwinding toward 52. No US macro release falls inside the window; CME equity index futures close early at 17:00 UTC and the next high-impact checkpoints are PPI on September 10 and CPI on September 11.
